title: feat: a fix test bar by severity, one security run, plan graphs
headline: A fix now needs a test that fails first when it is high, critical, security or an owner rule, and otherwise only when a real input shows the problem; CI states each fix test's verdict, runs the security tests once, and reads plans and rules as graphs.
alignment: v1.40.0 is build 14 of the v2.0 plan: K105, the sweep-fix test bar and the PR test run, with step T8, graphs where they pay.

items.text: A high, critical, security or owner-rule fix ships with a test that fails before it; a low or medium one gets a test only when a real input shows the problem, and its ledger row says `no test: no real input`.
items.after: A test only for a real input

items.text: The build record keeps one row per sweep fix (severity, commit and its test), refuses a high, critical, security or owner-rule row with no test, and writes the PR's fix-test line from the rows.
The test check states, for each test the fix rows name, whether it fails first on the code before the change, and names a fix whose test does not.
The test check reads tests made in a loop, and counts a new test in a file the old code cannot load as failing first; a changed file that cannot load is still named.
The test sort reads the tags above a loop for each test the loop makes, so the 69 merge-gate refusal tests sort as guards, not as repeats.
A mutation run gives its tests a throwaway home folder, so a flipped line can no longer rewrite the owner's install record.
A PR's changed run adds the security tests itself, so each runs once, and runs the whole suite when the change reaches over half of it.
`node .claude/plan-graph.mjs <plan>` names every pair of batch-plan units that may run at once and touch the same file, an order naming no unit, and an order cycle.
`scripts/rule-map.mjs` lists, for each rule, the guards, scripts, tests and workflows whose code names it, and the rules only prose holds; CI fails a stale map.
`test-run.mjs --changed --pick` prints the tests a change reaches without running them, and a unit brief takes its covering tests from it.

decisions.decision: The fix ledger lives in the committed build record
decisions.why: CI reads only what is committed; the sweep's own ledger stays the reviewers' raw list, in a folder git ignores.

decisions.decision: Tests made in a loop are run by their file
decisions.why: The harness filter takes exact names, and a loop's names exist only at run time; slower for a large file, right for every loop shape.
A read of the beads tool showed ordering only, no file fences, and a database, a binary and hooks of its own beside the guards.

verification: Each new check was seen failing on the code before it and passing after.
The rule lines were scored by the recall test against the released 1.39.0.
upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. A sweep's fixes now go in the build record as `sweep.fixes` rows, where a project keeps one.
limits: Whether a real input shows a low or medium problem is the lead's call, shown in the record; no script can tell. The rule map counts a name, not proof that the code holds the rule.
